Part 1 · Objectives, degrees of freedom and pairing

What must C-201 hold, how many handles does it have, and which valve should move which variable?

Part 1 · the plan

From objectives to pairings

  1. Control objectivesranked: safety, equipment, inventory, quality, throughput, energy
  2. The loop and the loopsset point, error, controller, valve, process, sensor; then the seven loops on the P&ID
  3. Degrees of freedom13 − 8 = 5 steady-state handles; seven valves, two spent on inventories
  4. Pairing reflux and boil-upgain matrix from the model and the relative gain λ = 1.37

Control objectives

Objectives come in a fixed order

A lower rank is never met by giving up a higher one. Ranks 1–2 belong to the relief valve, the SIS and auto-starts; the loops serve ranks 3–6.

Interactive · the feedback loop

Every block of the loop has a C-201 instance

Click the blocks: TIC-208 is reverse acting (hotter tray 8 → less steam), so the feedback is negative; the tray temperature stands in for the bottoms C3.

Interactive · loops on the P&ID

Seven loops, seven control valves

Click a bubble: heat and feed fail closed, reflux and vent fail open; the trip switches are separate from the loop transmitters.

Degrees of freedom (DOF)

Count the handles before choosing loops

$$N_{DOF}=N_{var}-N_{eq}=N_{dist}+N_{man}$$
$N_{var}$
steady-state variables: flows, duties, feed condition, pressure, blanketed area, purities, tray 8 temperature
–
$N_{eq}$
independent equations: preheater, total and light-key balances, tray model, condenser, inert balance, bubble point
–
$N_{dist}$
fixed by the surroundings: feed composition and temperature, inerts, cooling water, steam header
–
$N_{man}$
independent handles set continuously
–
$N_{DOF}=13-8=5$disturbances left out of the variable list
$N_{valves}-N_{inv}=7-2=5$sump and drum holdups have no steady-state effect

The five: FV-201, TV-202, TV-208, FV-204, PV-210. At most five variables set the steady state.

Interactive · DOF counter

Seven valves, five steady-state handles

Click each valve to drop it in its bin; a holdup needs its valve but leaves the steady state free.

Steady-state DOF0
Inventory only0

Five valves fix feed, preheat, boil-up, reflux and pressure; LV-202 and LV-203 must hold the levels but set nothing at steady state.

Interactive · what a loop does to the count

A loop spends one DOF; structures add none

Cascade and feedforward move the same valves; MAN hands a DOF to the operator; a saturated valve loses it and its CV drifts.

Interactive · model check

Five handles, five different fingerprints

One set point moved at a time, other loops in AUTO, 3 h on a copy of the model.

The effect matrix has rank 5. With tray 8 held, a feed or preheat change still moves both qualities.

Interactive · relative gain

Which composition should the reflux hold?

$$\lambda=\Big[1-\frac{g_{DV}\,g_{BL}}{g_{DL}\,g_{BV}}\Big]^{-1}$$

$g_{DL}$, $g_{DV}$: AI-219 (C4+ in propane) change per m³/h reflux, per % TV-208

$g_{BL}$, $g_{BV}$: the same for AI-220 (C3 in bottoms); model, 6 h

Model gains give λ = 1.37: reflux → top, boil-up → bottoms. The crossed pairing has 1 − λ = −0.37: closing one loop would reverse the other.

Section summary

What part 1 settled

  • Safety, equipment and inventories rank before quality, throughput and energy.
  • TIC-208 is reverse acting on a fail-closed valve; action and fail position are chosen separately.
  • C-201 has 13 − 8 = 5 steady-state DOF; seven valves, two of them spent on the levels.
  • A loop spends one DOF; cascade and feedforward add none; MAN or saturation takes it away.
  • λ = 1.37 pairs reflux with the top and boil-up with the bottoms.

Part 2 · Why tray 8 and the pressure loop

Why is the bottoms quality held on tray 8, and why is the pressure held first, by venting inerts?

Part 2 · the plan

From the temperature profile to the vent

  1. Tray sensitivitywhich trays answer the boil-up: ±0.5 % on TV-208, 6 h on the model
  2. Candidate trays under loadwhich held temperature keeps the bottoms near 1.00 % C3
  3. Pressure moves every temperatureabout 0.31 °C per 10 kPa on tray 8 at constant composition
  4. Venting the inertshow PV-210 sets the working area of E-202, and why the loop is slow

Interactive · tray sensitivity

Which trays answer the boil-up?

A 5 % step lowers the pressure 0.064 MPa, 63 % of it after about 15 min: PIC-210 needs a long reset and leaves fast rises to the relief valve.

Section summary

What part 2 settled

  • Trays 4–8 answer the boil-up; the sump and the rectifying trays barely move.
  • Holding tray 4 or 8 keeps the bottoms closest to 1 % C3; the sump fails on pressure, tray 12 on feed rate.
  • Pressure shifts every tray about 0.3 °C per 10 kPa, so PIC-210 comes first and TIC-227 stays in MAN.
  • PV-210 acts by venting inerts: slow (τ 744 s) and weaker as the condenser clears.

Part 3 · P, PI, PID and tuning

How is a gain read from a step test, and what do feedforward and averaging add?

Part 3 · the plan

From the controller equation to a tuned column

  1. The simulator's PIDideal form in % of span
  2. Two step-test modelssettling or ramping: tray 8 and the levels integrate
  3. Lambda tuning and the labchoose the speed, then run it on the model
  4. Feedforward and averaging levelmove before the error; let a level swing so the flows do not

Proportional-integral-derivative (PID)

The controller inside every C-201 faceplate

$$\mathrm{OUT}=K_c\Big[e+\frac{1}{T_i}\!\int e\,dt-T_d\frac{d\,\mathrm{PV}}{dt}\Big]+b$$
  • % of span: 1 °C on TIC-208 (0–150 °C) is only 0.67 %.
  • Derivative acts on PV: no kick on a set-point change.
  • Anti-windup at 0 and 100 %; bumpless on mode changes.
$e$
error SP − PV (reverse) or PV − SP (direct), in % of span
%
$K_c$
controller gain: % OUT per % error
%/%
$T_i$
reset (integral) time; $T_i=0$ means P only
s
$T_d$
rate (derivative) time, filtered by $T_d/8$
s
$b$
bias: the OUT held when the loop was closed
%

Step-test identification

Settles or ramps: two models from one step

$$G(s)=\frac{K\,e^{-\theta s}}{\tau s+1}\qquad G(s)=\frac{K'\,e^{-\theta s}}{s}$$
$K$
steady change of PV per change of OUT, both in % of span (first order plus dead time, FOPDT)
%/%
$K'$
ramp rate of PV per % of OUT (integrating process)
%/s per %
$\tau$, $\theta$
time constant; dead time before PV starts to move
s
$t_{28},\,t_{63}$
times to 28.3 % and 63.2 % of the final change
s
$K=\frac{-0.0636/2.5}{5}\cdot100=-0.509$PIC-210: ΔPV / ΔOUT in % of span
$\tau=1.5\,(922-426)=744\ \mathrm{s}$two-point fit $\tau = 1.5\,(t_{63}-t_{28})$
$\theta=922-744=178\ \mathrm{s}$$\theta = t_{63}-\tau$ (an apparent delay)
$K'=\frac{0.00602/150}{2}\cdot100=0.0020$TIC-208: steepest slope (°C/s) of a 2 % step

From the previous slide$K e^{-\theta s}/(\tau s+1)$  or  $K' e^{-\theta s}/s$
Model fit
Your misfit

Flows, preheat and pressure settle; tray 8 and the sump ramp: 2 % more steam heats tray 8 0.36 °C per min at first, and 10.8 °C after 40 min.

Interactive · lambda (IMC) tuning

Choose the closed-loop speed, get the gain

$$\begin{gathered}K_c=\frac{\tau}{K(\lambda+\theta)},\quad T_i=\tau\\ K_c=\frac{1}{K'(\lambda+\theta)},\quad T_i=4(\lambda+\theta)\end{gathered}$$

$\lambda$: chosen closed-loop time constant (s), internal model control (IMC); top settling, bottom integrating

Lambda PI
Simulator

TIC-208's simulator gain 3 sits between smooth (1.63) and tight (7.59); PIC-210 runs at 6, above both lambda gains, and overshoots 43 % on a set-point step.

Interactive · tuning lab on the model

Four tunings, five loops, one model

Feed +5 %: P only leaves tray 8 0.39 °C off; tight lambda cuts the dip 1.48 → 0.66 °C by moving TV-208 more. Dashed: simulator tuning.

Interactive · feedforward (recommended addition FY-201)

Move steam and reflux with the feed, with a lag

Feed 60 → 63 m³/h, simulator tuning; reflux SP = 49 × F/60 (assumed rule).

Unlagged reflux is worse than none (dip 3.68 °C): it reaches tray 8 before the feed does. Lagged, the dip falls 1.48 → 1.03 °C.

Interactive · averaging level control

Let the sump swing so the bottoms flow does not

A level integrates inflow minus outflow; how fast LIC-202 answers decides where a feed step goes.

Integrating lambda rule$K_c=1/[K'(\lambda+\theta)]$, $T_i=4(\lambda+\theta)$
Tuning
Sump rise
Bottoms flow peak
Fastest flow change

Feed +3 m³/h: λ 600 s lets the sump rise 1.9 % and ramps the bottoms 0.23 m³/h per min; λ 150 s holds 0.7 % but ramps 3× faster.

Section summary

What part 3 settled

  • The PID works in % of span, derivative on PV, with anti-windup.
  • Flows, preheat and pressure fit $K$, $\tau$, $\theta$; tray 8 and the levels fit a ramp $K'$, $\theta$.
  • Lambda PI turns the fit and a chosen $\lambda$ into $K_c$ and $T_i$; P only leaves an offset.
  • Feedforward helps only with the right dynamics; averaging level control trades level swing for smooth flow.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Rank the objectives and count the degrees of freedom before drawing a loop.

2

Pair by gains: check the relative gain before closing two composition loops.

3

Control on the tray that answers composition, not pressure; hold pressure first.

4

Fit a step test, then choose $\lambda$: slow processes and dead time limit the gain.

5

Tune levels for averaging and give feedforward the process's own lag.
